question: Which item of PPE must be worn in every ME-106 shop?
options: Workshop apron
Ear muffs
Welding helmet
Laser goggles
explanation: The ME-106 log sheets and slides for the machine shops, grinding, milling and electroplating all ask for the workshop apron.
ref: Log Sheets ME-106 p.1, p.4, p.7

question: Why are closed safety (leather) shoes required in the workshop?
options: They insulate the wearer from every electric shock
They keep the workshop floor clean
They make walking between machines faster
They protect the feet from falling objects and hot chips
explanation: Proper shoes protect feet from dropped tools, jobs and hot chips.

question: Why must loose clothing be avoided near machines?
options: It slows down the speed of the work
It affects the accuracy of measurements
It can be caught by rotating parts
It gets dirty with coolant and oil
explanation: Loose sleeves, ties and clothes can be pulled into chucks, cutters and spindles.

question: Which of these should be removed before working on a machine?
options: Safety shoes with steel toe caps
Rings, bracelets, chains and wristwatches
Workshop apron, tied at the back
Safety goggles with side shields
explanation: Loose accessories can be caught by moving parts.
ref: Log Sheets ME-106 p.7; Milling TA slides s.2

question: What should a student with long hair do before operating a machine?
options: Wet it with coolant so it stays down
Tie it back or cover it
Tuck it under the apron strap only
Leave it loose behind the shoulders
explanation: Long hair can be caught in rotating parts.

question: Safety goggles are especially needed when…
options: Reading the log sheet
Measuring with a steel rule
Writing calculations
Chips, sparks or splashes can fly
explanation: Grinding, chipping, filing and plating can throw particles or liquids.
ref: Fitting lecture s.13; Theory: Hajra Choudhury

question: Why should gloves NOT be worn near rotating parts such as a lathe chuck?
options: They can be caught and pull the hand in
They damage the chuck
They reduce the cutting speed
They make the job slippery to measure
explanation: A glove snagged by a rotating part drags the hand in.

question: You may operate a workshop machine only…
options: Whenever the shop happens to be open
If a friend has shown you how it works
With the instructor's permission and supervision
After hours when the shop is quiet
explanation: Do not operate the machine without supervision from the shop instructor.
ref: Milling TA slides s.2; Grinding PPT s.2

question: While a machine is running, you should…
options: Stay alert and avoid talking or fooling around
Use your phone between the cuts
Leave it running while you fetch tools
Lean on it to watch the cut closely
explanation: Stay attentive during fixing and cutting.

question: Where should you stand while a machine runs?
options: In line with the ram or wheel
As close as possible to the cutter
On the machine base
At a safe distance from moving parts
explanation: Maintain a proper distance from the running machine.

question: Before measuring or adjusting a job on a machine, you must…
options: Engage the feed
Remove the guard
Stop the machine
Increase the speed
explanation: Always stop the machine before measuring, cleaning, adjusting or changing tools.
ref: Log Sheets ME-106 p.3; Theory: Hajra Choudhury

question: In case of trouble on a machine, the first thing to do is…
options: Run to fetch the instructor
Press the emergency stop / switch off
Pull the job out by hand
Increase the feed to finish quickly
explanation: Know where the emergency stop is and use it at once.

question: Is it acceptable to leave a running machine unattended?
options: Only when the job is small
Only when the coolant is on
Only for a minute or two
No, never
explanation: Never leave a running machine unattended.

question: Before starting the machine, the job and tool must be…
options: Painted with chalk
Clamped firmly
Oiled heavily
Loosely held for adjustment
explanation: Loose work or tools can be thrown out.

question: Chips and swarf should be removed with…
options: A brush or chip hook, after stopping the machine
Bare hands while the cut is going on
A wet cloth while the job is turning
Compressed air blown towards others
explanation: Chips are sharp and hot.
ref: Log Sheets ME-106 p.1; Theory: Hajra Choudhury

question: Which electrical safety rule applies in the workshop?
options: Open panels to reset faults yourself
Use bare wires for quick connections
Never touch switches or connections with wet hands
Bypass the earth wire if the breaker trips
explanation: Water conducts electricity; do not touch electrical connections.

question: Heavy machine parts and tools should be…
options: Moved by one person always
Left on the machine bed
Handled with care
Thrown onto the bench
explanation: Handle heavy machines and tools with care.

question: Why must the floor around machines be kept clean?
options: Oil and chips on the floor cause slips and falls
It reduces the amount of coolant used
It keeps the machine motor cooler
It improves the surface finish of jobs
explanation: Keep the area free of oil, chips and obstacles.

question: After finishing work on a machine, you should…
options: Leave the chips for the next batch
Leave tools on the bed
Keep the machine running
Clean it and return the tools to their place
explanation: Clean the machine and workspace after use.

question: Which is a basic rule about tools?
options: Any tool will do for any job
Use the right tool and never a damaged one
Borrow tools without asking
Damaged tools are fine for practice
explanation: Use the correct tool; do not use damaged tools.

question: What should you do if you get even a small cut in the workshop?
options: Cover it with chalk to stop the bleeding
Ignore it and keep working until done
Report it to the instructor and get first aid
Wash it in the coolant tank and carry on
explanation: Report every injury; know where the first-aid box is.

question: Which extinguisher should be used on an electrical or oil fire?
options: Sand mixed with oil
CO₂ or dry powder
Water
A wet cloth
explanation: Never use water on electrical or oil fires; water is for ordinary combustibles.

question: Water-type fire extinguishers are suitable only for…
options: Oil and fuel fires
Burning metal fires
Electrical equipment fires
Ordinary combustibles like wood and paper
explanation: Water conducts electricity and spreads oil fires.

question: In safety colour codes, a solid blue circular sign means…
options: A mandatory instruction (must do)
Safe condition / first aid
Danger / stop
Caution / warning
explanation: Red = stop/prohibition/fire, yellow = caution, green = safe/first aid, blue = mandatory.

question: In safety colour codes, green indicates…
options: Mandatory action
Danger / prohibition
Caution / warning
Safe condition, first aid or exit
explanation: Green = safe condition or first aid.

question:
Assertion (A): Gloves must not be worn near rotating machine parts.
Reason (R): A glove caught by a rotating part can drag the hand in.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
explanation: Both true, and R explains A.

question: How should a heavy job be lifted from the floor?
options: Lift it above the head before carrying it
Bend the knees, keep the back straight, get help if needed
Bend the back and lift fast with straight legs
Drag it along the floor by one corner
explanation: Lifting with the legs, not the back, prevents back injury; heavy or awkward loads need help.

question: First aid for a minor burn from a hot chip is to…
options: Cool it under clean running water for some minutes
Keep working and ignore it till the end
Cover it tightly with dry cotton wool
Rub grease or machine oil on the burn
explanation: Cool the burn with running water; never apply grease or oil, and report it.

question: If plating solution splashes into your eye, you should first…
options: Rub the eye hard with the back of your hand
Wait for the stinging to stop on its own
Rinse the eye with plenty of clean water for 15 minutes
Wipe it with a dry cloth and carry on working
explanation: Flush immediately and continuously with clean water (eye-wash), then report it.

question: Which use of compressed air is UNSAFE in the workshop?
options: Operating an air-powered clamp
Blowing chips off clothes or towards other people
Supplying assist gas to the laser head
Driving a pneumatic tool as intended
explanation: Compressed air can drive particles into eyes and skin; never point it at people or clothes.

question: Gangways and emergency exits in the workshop must be…
options: Used to store jobs and tools
Locked while machines are running
Blocked with benches for safety
Kept clear at all times
explanation: Clear exits and gangways allow escape in an emergency.

question: While a friend is operating a lathe, you should…
options: Not distract or startle them
Tap their shoulder to talk
Lean on the machine beside them
Hand them tools over the chuck
explanation: Distracting an operator can cause a serious accident.

question: What does sign A indicate?
options: Safe condition / first aid
Warning (caution)
Prohibition (do not)
Radiation hazard only
explanation: A = Prohibition (do not). Red ring with a diagonal bar: forbids an action.
label: A

question: What does sign B indicate?
options: Radiation hazard only
Warning (caution)
Fire equipment location
Prohibition (do not)
explanation: B = Warning (caution). Yellow triangle with black border: warns of a hazard.
label: B

question: What does sign C indicate?
options: Fire equipment location
Safe condition / first aid
Mandatory instruction (must do)
Prohibition (do not)
explanation: C = Mandatory instruction (must do). Solid blue circle: something you must do, e.g. wear goggles.
label: C

question: What does sign D indicate?
options: Mandatory instruction (must do)
Fire equipment location
Radiation hazard only
Safe condition / first aid
explanation: D = Safe condition / first aid. Green rectangle: first aid, emergency exit, safe condition.
label: D

question: Which sign is used for a safe condition / first aid?
options: D
A
B
C
explanation: D = Safe condition / first aid. Green rectangle: first aid, emergency exit, safe condition.
label: D
